summary: The ladder goes from last quarter's gross revenue to each store's share and monthly trend. It then shows that the established stores are slipping because customers visit less often while the new stores are still ramping up, and it ends by sizing three levers for next quarter: visit frequency, basket size and growth at the new stores.

narration.text: Gross revenue in the last complete quarter, Q3 2026, was $649.1K, which is the base that next quarter's growth has to build on.
Brooklyn brought in $318.1K of that, Philadelphia $195.4K, Chicago $79.5K and San Francisco $56.1K.
Month by month, Brooklyn peaked at $115.8K in July and fell to $84.7K by October, while Philadelphia slipped from $71.0K to $55.3K over the same stretch.
The two stores that opened in July are moving the other way, with Chicago up to $36.5K and San Francisco to $32.0K in October.

The slide in Brooklyn and Philadelphia comes mostly from fewer visits per customer, not fewer customers or smaller baskets: Brooklyn's orders per customer fell from 15.6 in July to 12.8 in September while its customer count held near 698, and Philadelphia's dropped from 14.0 to 11.4.
October then shows a drop in customers, to 548 in Brooklyn and 360 in Philadelphia, while average order value stayed close to $10.32 and $11.42.
Even so, both stores remain ahead of last year, with Brooklyn up 62.2% in October and Philadelphia up 13.1%, so the slowdown is a loss of momentum rather than a collapse.

Focus first on winning back visit frequency at Brooklyn and Philadelphia, since the Q3 levers table shows Brooklyn's 699 customers at $455.0 revenue each and Philadelphia's 449 at $435.3, against $311.6 at Chicago and $265.9 at San Francisco.
Test a push on jaffle attach at Brooklyn, Chicago and San Francisco, because Philadelphia sells 1.51 jaffle units per order against 1.41 in Brooklyn, 1.45 in Chicago and 1.38 in San Francisco.
Keep the new-store customer ramp going at Chicago and San Francisco, where customers reached 257 and 228 in October and San Francisco added 8.1% on the month.

digests.question: Which stores drive revenue?
digests.headline: Brooklyn leads, new stores rising
digests.summary: Gross revenue in Q3 2026 was $649.1K, with Brooklyn and Philadelphia supplying most of it. Both are declining since July, while Chicago and San Francisco, which opened in July, are growing.

digests.question: Why are established stores slipping?
digests.headline: fewer visits per customer
digests.summary: Gross revenue in Q3 2026 was $649.1K, led by Brooklyn and Philadelphia, which have slipped since July while the new Chicago and San Francisco stores grow. The slide comes mainly from fewer visits per customer, with October also losing customers, though both stores are still above last year.

digests.question: What should we do?
digests.headline: frequency, basket, new stores
digests.summary: Gross revenue in Q3 2026 was $649.1K, led by Brooklyn and Philadelphia, which have slipped since July on fewer visits per customer, while Chicago and San Francisco keep growing. Next quarter's growth should come from winning back visit frequency at the two established stores, lifting jaffle attach towards Philadelphia's level, and sustaining the new stores' customer ramp.
